name: Chevening Scholarships
description: UK government-funded awards for eligible one-year taught master’s degrees.
requirements: Requires eligible citizenship, an undergraduate degree, at least 2,800 hours of post-graduation work experience, applications to three eligible UK courses, and a commitment to return to your country of citizenship for at least two years after the award.

name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program
description: Supports graduate study and research in the United States. Award coverage and duration depend on the applicant’s home-country program.
requirements: For applicants from participating non-U.S. countries. Academic, citizenship, English-language and application requirements vary by home country; some grants have a two-year home-country physical-presence condition under U.S. visa rules.
income: Not generally an income-band award; country-level funding rules vary.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
description: Selected international joint master’s programs may offer scholarships contributing to participation, travel, visa, and living costs.
requirements: Applicants normally need a bachelor’s degree or be in their final undergraduate year and graduate before the master’s starts. Each consortium sets its own admission rules and participating study locations.
income: Selection is not based on a universal household-income band.

name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
description: Full-cost postgraduate funding for outstanding applicants from outside the United Kingdom at the University of Cambridge.
requirements: Must be a citizen of a country outside the UK and apply for an eligible full-time postgraduate course at Cambridge. Academic excellence, course fit, leadership and commitment to improving others’ lives matter.

name: Clarendon Scholarships
description: Competitive graduate scholarships at Oxford covering course fees and a grant for living costs.
requirements: Apply by the relevant December or January course deadline for an eligible Oxford graduate course. Selection is based on academic merit and potential; no separate Clarendon application is generally required.

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
description: Graduate fellowship supporting eligible study at Stanford across disciplines.
requirements: Requires a separate Knight-Hennessy application and admission to an eligible full-time Stanford graduate program. Applicants must meet the current first-bachelor’s-degree recency window; check the official year-specific rule.
income: Not restricted to a universal income band.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies
description: DAAD funding opportunities for international graduates pursuing eligible master’s study in Germany.
requirements: Rules differ by country, course, call and scholarship line; check degree recency, language evidence and any relevant professional experience in the DAAD database.
income: Some DAAD calls consider personal circumstances; no single income cutoff applies to all awards.

name: Australia Awards Scholarships
description: Long-term study and development awards for citizens of participating countries.
requirements: Only eligible participating-country citizens can apply. Applicants generally must be at least 18 by 1 February of the scholarship year and agree to leave Australia for at least two years after completing the award. Country priorities and study levels vary.
income: Eligibility is determined by country-specific rules rather than a global income band.

name: Türkiye Scholarships
description: Government scholarships for eligible international students across undergraduate and graduate levels.
requirements: Published age and academic-achievement thresholds depend on degree level; nationality and program restrictions apply. Check the current application call for exact cutoffs and exceptions.
income: No universal household-income cutoff is published for every award.

name: Reach Oxford Scholarship
description: Undergraduate funding for eligible students from low-income countries who cannot study for a degree in their own countries for political or financial reasons or because suitable facilities do not exist.
requirements: Requires an Oxford undergraduate offer and citizenship of an eligible country; medicine is excluded. Strong academic ability and financial need are considered. Check the official country list and application process.
income: Financial need is a key consideration, but there is no universal USD household-income cutoff.

name: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship
description: A competitive undergraduate scholarship for international students with exceptional academic achievement, creativity and leadership.
requirements: For eligible international secondary-school students entering first-year undergraduate study; school nomination and University of Toronto application are required. Check current graduation-year rules.
income: Award is not based on a universal household-income threshold.

name: Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals
description: Scholarships for eligible master’s applicants from selected countries with leadership and professional experience.
requirements: Citizenship must be on the current eligible-country list; eligible master’s admission, documented work experience and leadership experience are generally required. Country-specific rules apply.

requirements: International applicant (non-citizen, no U.S. permanent residency) with interest in intercultural learning; apply by Feb 1.

name: Temple #WhyUS Scholarship
description: $2,000-$10,000 per year awards based on a creative response to a prompt rather than academics.
requirements: Temple international applicant; submit creative response by March 1; check official page.

name: Temple Sister City Scholarship
description: $10,000 per year for four years for first-year students from Philadelphia's sister cities.
requirements: Must be from a listed Philadelphia sister city (e.g. Florence, Frankfurt, Incheon, Kobe, Tianjin, Tel Aviv-Yafo); check official page.

name: Tulane International Merit Scholarships
description: Merit awards up to full tuition for outstanding admitted international students.
requirements: Non-U.S. citizen not eligible for U.S. federal aid; Common App, CSS Profile and Declaration & Certification of Finances required.

name: Emory University Scholars (International Merit)
description: Highly competitive merit scholarships offered to a limited number of international first-years each year.
requirements: Citizen of a foreign country and not a U.S. permanent resident; apply through the Emory Scholar programs before December; check official page.

name: Emory Need-Based Aid for International Undergraduates
description: Need-based financial aid for admitted international students under Regular Decision.
requirements: Apply for aid on the Common App, submit CSS Profile and tax documents by Feb 5; limited funding.
income: Need-based; must demonstrate financial need via CSS Profile.

name: GWU You Are Welcome Here Scholarship
description: Two full-tuition awards each year for first-year international applicants committed to bridging intercultural divides.
requirements: First-year fall applicant; essay or video response and CSS Profile required.

name: GWU Presidential Academic Scholarships (International)
description: Merit scholarships for which strong international first-year applicants are automatically considered.
requirements: Strong academic credentials; value varies; GW offers no need-based aid to international applicants.

name: Davis UWC Scholars at George Washington University
description: Need-based awards up to full tuition and fees for UWC graduates admitted to GW.
requirements: Graduate of a United World College; CSS Profile required; award varies by need.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: University of Cincinnati International Outreach Award
description: Annual awards of $5,000-$15,000 (Uptown) or $2,000-$4,000 (regional campuses) for international undergraduates.
requirements: 3.0 unweighted GPA minimum, non-resident tuition payer; no separate application; apply by Nov 1 for first-years.

name: University of Tulsa International Academic Award
description: Four-year partial tuition awards of $1,000-$10,000 based on high school academics and English proficiency.
requirements: Admitted international first-year; amount tied to GPA and IELTS/TOEFL; check official page.

name: University of Tulsa Presidential Scholarship (International)
description: Full-tuition scholarship for eight semesters for top international applicants.
requirements: 4.0 GPA and separate application with resume; check official page.

name: University of Tulsa Global Ambassador Award
description: $3,000 or $5,000 award for four years, stackable with the Academic Award.
requirements: Recognized competition participation and leadership; check official page.

name: University of Tulsa #YouAreWelcomeHere Scholarship
description: 50% tuition for up to four years; two awards for first-year undergraduates.
requirements: Separate application with essay or video; deadline typically March; check official page.

name: University of St. Thomas International Merit Scholarships
description: Merit tuition scholarships of 10-70% renewable for up to four years for international undergraduates.
requirements: Renewable with 2.0+ GPA; tuition only; confirm current deadlines with International Admissions.

name: St. Thomas GHR Fellows Program (International)
description: Full-tuition scholarship for business majors selected through a values-based process.
requirements: High school GPA at least 3.7 and business major; check official page.

name: Marquette Global Scholar Award
description: Full tuition, housing, food and fees for one international high school senior each year, renewable up to eight semesters.
requirements: Outside-U.S. high school, 3.25 unweighted GPA, F-1 status, leadership; essay and video interview; apply by March 1.

name: Vanderbilt Need-Based Aid for International First-Years
description: Need-based scholarships for a limited number of first-year international undergraduates.
requirements: Indicate need on application; CSS Profile or ISFAA by deadline; need-aware; transfers ineligible.
income: Need-based; need-aware admission for international applicants.

name: Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship (Vanderbilt)
description: Full tuition plus summer stipend and travel allowance for Finnish students in the College of Arts and Science.
requirements: Finnish student with financial need; CSS Profile or ISFAA required.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: Irene and Thomas Harrington International Scholarship (Vanderbilt)
description: Scholarship for international undergraduates in any school, with preference for France then the EU.
requirements: CSS Profile or ISFAA required; check official page for need criteria.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: Early-White International Scholarship (Vanderbilt)
description: Scholarship for UK or EU students in the College of Arts and Science.
requirements: UK or EU student; CSS Profile or ISFAA required.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: Wright State UCIE Undergraduate Merit Scholarship
description: $6,000-$10,000 per year merit awards for international undergraduates based on GPA.
requirements: GPA 2.5 or higher; F-1/J-1 non-resident tuition payers; no application needed.

name: Wright State International Ambassador Scholarship
description: $10,000 per year for two first-year international students living on campus.
requirements: First-year on-campus resident; apply by March 12; check official page.

name: Wright State Southeast Asia Merit Scholarship
description: $12,000 per year for F-1 students from listed Southeast Asian high schools (a Vietnam-specific version also exists).
requirements: Attended high school in a listed Southeast Asian country; check official page for list.

name: Carleton College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Carleton meets 100% of demonstrated need without loans for admitted international students, with limited international aid funding.
requirements: Apply with ISAFA or CSS Profile before admission offer; Certification of Finances required.
income: Need-based; no income caps stated by the college.

name: UC Berkeley Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship (International)
description: Highest Berkeley undergraduate scholarship; admitted international first-years and transfers are automatically considered.
requirements: Exceptional students showing creativity, leadership, service; no separate application.

name: Robinson International Scholars Program (UC Berkeley)
description: Need-based scholarship for up to four years for refugees/stateless individuals or students from Sub-Saharan Africa and developing nations.
requirements: Refugee or stateless, or completed secondary school in an eligible region; no separate application; check official page.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: International Leaders Scholarship (UC Berkeley)
description: Need-based award for up to four years for academically excellent international students with leadership potential; priority for Peruvian residents.
requirements: Admitted international undergraduate; no separate application; check official page.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: Swaniker Scholars Program (UC Berkeley)
description: Need-based awards up to full cost of attendance for four years for African students nominated from ALX Pathway or African Leadership Academy.
requirements: Nominated African student; check official page.
income: Need-based; check official page for how need is assessed.

name: University of Minnesota Global Excellence Scholarships
description: Competitive merit awards for international freshmen and transfer students; all on-time applicants are automatically considered.
requirements: Apply by deadline; no separate application; no full-tuition award offered.

name: University of Michigan LSA International Student Scholarship
description: Scholarship for admitted international first-year or transfer students in LSA, renewable for two to four years.
requirements: Admitted to LSA for Fall, full-time, not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; also considers grades and financial need; deadline April 9.
income: Awards consider financial need alongside academics.

name: University of Mary Washington International Merit Scholarships
description: Automatic merit awards of $1,000-$9,000 for admitted international students (Presidential-Honors through Aerie), plus a $4,000 Global Scholar Award for F-1 students.
requirements: Admitted international student; based on GPA and test scores; living on campus required.

name: Colorado State University International Undergraduate Scholarships
description: $2,000-$12,000 per year automatic awards for admitted international undergraduates, renewable for four years.
requirements: Strong GPA and rigorous coursework; apply by Dec 15 for highest consideration.

name: University of Missouri International Honors and International Merit Scholarships
description: Freshman awards of $20,000 (Honors) or $10,000 (Merit) per year, plus transfer awards for international students.
requirements: Admission application, English proficiency, SAT/ACT preferred; check official page.

name: Texas A&M International Student Scholarships
description: Set of departmental-level scholarships for enrolled international students including Eppright, Goodman International Fund and Good Neighbor awards.
requirements: Full-time, GPR minimums (3.0 undergrad/3.5 grad for some); several need-based; J-1 holders ineligible for ITPEG; check official page.
income: Several awards require demonstrated financial need.

name: University of South Florida Green and Gold International Scholarships
description: Tuition waivers worth up to $11,000 per year (Presidential, Directors, Scholars tiers) for admitted international first-years.
requirements: Automatically considered if freshman application is complete by Jan 15; limited number.

name: Wayne State University International Merit Awards (Warrior, Gold, Green)
description: Academic merit scholarships for new international first-year undergraduates; all admitted students are considered.
requirements: No U.S. citizenship needed; amounts not listed, check official page.

name: Utah Tech International Freshmen Merit Scholarship
description: $5,500 first-year tuition scholarship for new F-1 degree-seeking freshmen.
requirements: 3.0 GPA, ACT 26+ or SAT 1240+, English test score; maintain 3.3 GPA.

name: Utah Tech International Merit Scholarship (Continuing/Transfer)
description: $5,500 per year tuition scholarship for continuing or transfer F-1 students at the St. George campus.
requirements: 24+ credits and 3.3 GPA; good standing with ISSO.

name: Coe College International Merit Scholarships
description: Merit scholarships up to $16,000 per year, renewable for three years, based on high school academics and exams.
requirements: International applicant admitted to Coe; check official page.

name: Coe College Global Leadership Scholarship
description: One full-tuition award each year for a non-U.S. citizen high school graduate from outside the U.S., renewable.
requirements: First-time college student living on campus; separate application by Feb 15, 2027.

name: Berea College International Student Aid (Tuition Promise)
description: Admitted international students receive aid and scholarships covering 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees at Berea College.
requirements: Holistic admission based on academics, financial need, ambition, purpose and recommendations; students must work at least 10 hours/week in the Work Program; $2,200 deposit (adjustable); application due Nov 30; check official page.
income: Admission considers financial need; designed for students with limited financial means (no exact income figure published).

name: Amherst College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Amherst admits international students need-blind and states it meets 100% of calculated financial need with grants, not initially packaged loans.
requirements: Apply for aid with the admission application; forms per the Amherst financial aid office; check official page for CSS Profile details and deadlines.

name: Middlebury College Financial Aid for International Students
description: Middlebury awards need-based financial aid; international students may have need considered in admission and aid is determined via the CSS Profile.
requirements: Apply for aid with admission application; CSS Profile plus tax documents; check official page or contact sfs@middlebury.edu for international specifics.

name: Davidson College Alvarez Scholars Program
description: Davidson commits to meeting 100% of calculated need for admitted international students; all international aid applicants are considered for Alvarez Scholars need-based scholarships.
requirements: Apply for aid at the time of admission application (none after admission); Financial Verification Form for all, then CSS Profile ($25, no waivers) or alternative form if expected family contribution under $5,000.

name: USC Merit Scholarships (Trustee, Presidential, Deans)
description: USC's Office of Admission awards Trustee, Presidential and Deans merit scholarships to admitted first-year students, valued relative to flat-rate tuition.
requirements: Apply Early Decision/Early Action by Nov 1 for merit consideration; no separate application; international eligibility details are on USC's international section, check official page.

name: Duke Karsh International Scholars Program
description: Karsh International Scholars receive funding for tuition, room and board, fees and demonstrated need above those costs, plus three summers of funding for research or internships.
requirements: Non-U.S. citizens (not dual U.S. citizens) with demonstrated need and strong academics; no separate application, apply to Duke and request aid; cannot be nominated.

name: Duke Need-Based Aid for International Undergraduates
description: Duke provides need-based aid to admitted international undergraduates; no federal loans are available to them.
requirements: Check the financial aid interest box on the admission application; not available to international transfer students; see Awarding & Policy page.

name: Boston University Presidential Scholarship (International Eligible)
description: Half-tuition merit scholarship for first-year students entering Fall 2026; open to U.S. citizens, permanent residents and international students.
requirements: Complete the BU admission application by December 1; no separate application; strong academics plus leadership and impact.

name: Wellesley College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Wellesley is committed to meeting 100% of calculated need for admitted international citizens who applied for aid during admission.
requirements: Indicate aid on admission application; complete Financial Aid Intent Form and CSS Profile when requested; funds are limited; check official page for deadlines.

name: Smith College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Smith awards need-based Smith Grants to non-U.S. citizens; merit aid is offered only at the time of admission.
requirements: Apply for aid by admission deadline: CSS PROFILE (code 3762) and translated parent tax documents; ED1 Nov 15, ED2 Jan 6, RD Jan 25.

name: Colby College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Colby meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international students.
requirements: CSS Profile (code 3280) required; fee waiver available; deadlines ED1 Nov 15, ED2 Jan 4, RD Jan 15.

name: Bowdoin College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Bowdoin meets full demonstrated need for admitted international students through scholarships and a small on-campus work expectation.
requirements: Non-Canadian international applicants submit aid materials only if admitted, within seven days of offer; check official page for forms.

name: NYU Scholarships for International First-Year Students
description: NYU offers scholarships and need-based aid to non-U.S. citizen first-year applicants based on the CSS Profile.
requirements: Submit CSS Profile by deadline; transfer and second-bachelor's applicants are not eligible; check official page for deadlines.

name: Dartmouth Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Dartmouth is need-blind for all international applicants and meets the demonstrated need of all admitted undergraduates, including a U.S. travel allowance.
requirements: Apply for aid with admission application; $1,500 student work contribution from later years for most non-Canadian international students; check official page.

name: Yale Financial Aid for International Students
description: Yale is need-blind for all applicants and meets 100% of demonstrated need with scholarship grants, not loans, regardless of citizenship.
requirements: CSS Profile required; Early Action Dec 1 and Regular Decision Feb 15 for international citizens.

name: Princeton Financial Aid for International Students
description: Princeton is need-blind, meets full demonstrated need of admitted international students with grants that need not be repaid; no merit scholarships.
requirements: Apply for aid with admission; see financial aid program information for forms and deadlines.

name: MIT Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: MIT meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for international undergraduates.
requirements: CSS Profile (code 3514) and parental income documents via IDOC; check official page for deadlines.

name: Bates College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Bates meets full demonstrated need of admitted non-U.S. citizens for up to eight semesters with grants and campus work, no loans.
requirements: Indicate intent to apply for aid on the admission application; submit the Bates International Student Application for Financial Aid (BISAFA); not need-blind.

name: Mount Holyoke College Merit and Need-Based Aid (International)
description: All international applicants are automatically considered for merit aid; need-based aid is available with the CSS Profile.
requirements: No separate merit application; need-based applicants submit CSS Profile and parental income documents; non-aid students submit the International Financial Declaration.
income: Merit has no ceiling; need-based aid depends on demonstrated need.

name: Bryn Mawr College Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Bryn Mawr meets the full calculated need of admitted international students, though it is need-sensitive and funds are limited.
requirements: CSS Profile (code 2049) and Declaration of Finances form with the application; ED1 Nov 15, ED2 Jan 1, RD Jan 15.

name: Wesleyan University Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Wesleyan meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students, including international students, though admission for aid-seeking internationals is highly competitive.
requirements: Apply for aid at the time of application: CSS Profile (code 3959) or ISFAA; no fee waivers; check official page for current deadlines.

name: Wesleyan African Scholars Program
description: Full four-year awards at Wesleyan for aid applicants who are citizens or permanent residents of African countries.
requirements: Citizens or permanent residents of African countries applying for aid; check official page for details.

name: Freeman Asian Scholarship Program (Wesleyan)
description: Full four-year awards at Wesleyan for aid applicants from listed Asian countries including China, Japan and India.
requirements: Citizenship or permanent residence in a listed Asian country; check official page for the full country list.

name: Grinnell College Aid and Merit Scholarships for International Students
description: Grinnell meets 100% of institutionally determined need for admitted international students and may award merit scholarships to outstanding applicants regardless of need.
requirements: CSS Profile or Grinnell's International Student Application for Financial Assistance by application deadline (Nov 15, Jan 5, Jan 15); aid cannot be requested later if not applied initially.
income: Need-based aid depends on demonstrated need; merit has no ceiling.

name: Macalester Charles J. Turck Presidential Honor Scholarship
description: Merit scholarship of up to $40,000 per year for a limited number of students; all international applicants are considered automatically.
requirements: No separate application; apply for admission by deadline (Nov 10, Jan 8, Jan 22).

name: Macalester Need-Based Aid for International Students
description: Need-based awards for international students, including part-time campus work.
requirements: Submit CSS Profile or ISAFA plus Macalester Financial Declaration Form; no fee waivers; aid is limited and competitive.

name: Oberlin Eduardo Chivambo Mondlane Scholarship
description: Merit scholarship of up to $10,000 for citizens of sub-Saharan African countries applying to Oberlin's College of Arts and Sciences.
requirements: No separate application; selected by admissions on academic record and potential.

name: Oberlin Edwin O. Reischauer Scholarship
description: Merit scholarship of up to $10,000 for Japanese nationals admitted to Oberlin's College of Arts and Sciences.
requirements: No separate application; selected by admissions.

name: Oberlin Yakubu Saaka Memorial Fund
description: $10,000 per year for four years for citizens of African countries applying to Oberlin's College of Arts and Sciences.
requirements: No separate application; selected by admissions on academic record.

name: Rotary Global Grant Scholarships
description: Graduate scholarships sponsored by Rotary clubs and districts for study abroad in one of Rotary's areas of focus (peace, disease, water, maternal and child health, education, local economies, environment). Can cover one to four years of study.
requirements: Graduate study abroad aligned with a Rotary area of focus; applicants apply through a sponsoring Rotary club or district; check official page for amounts and local deadlines.

name: AAUW International Fellowships
description: Funds women who are non-US citizens for a first master's ($20,000) or first doctorate ($25,000) in a STEM field at an accredited US institution.
requirements: Woman; non-US citizen without permanent residency; degree equivalent to a US bachelor's; minimum 3.5/4.0 GPA; first master's or doctorate in STEM; TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS 6.5; two recommendations; admission proof. Check official page for the current cycle.
income: Financial plan is assessed but no universal household-income ceiling.

name: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship
description: Awards of up to $12,500 for international women pursuing graduate study at accredited US or Canadian institutions.
requirements: Woman living outside the US and Canada; not a US/Canadian citizen or permanent resident; full year of formal coursework remaining; must plan to return home; applications Sep 15 to Dec 15.
income: Awarded based on demonstrated need; applicants must show other funding for estimated costs.

name: Zonta Amelia Earhart Fellowship
description: US$10,000 awarded annually to women of any nationality pursuing a PhD in aerospace engineering or space sciences at any accredited university.
requirements: Woman of any nationality; full-time PhD in aerospace engineering or space sciences; superior academic record; completed at least one year of the program or holds an aerospace-applied master's; check official page for current cycle.

name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
description: Half-grant, half-loan funding for postgraduate study (priority to master's, PhD considered) for students from selected developing countries; study in Canada, Portugal or the USA is allowed.
requirements: Applicant from a participating country (e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda); excellent academic record; admission to a reputable institution; preference under 30; apply through local contacts.
income: Awarded on genuine financial need; resource of last resort.

name: Stanford Graduate Fellowship in Science and Engineering
description: Multi-year stipend and tuition fellowship for incoming and current doctoral students in science, engineering and related fields, awarded to about 100 students per year.
requirements: Nomination only by an eligible Stanford degree program; doctoral level; check official page regarding international student status.

name: Frank Knox Memorial Fellowship (Harvard)
description: Fellowship for graduate students from Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United Kingdom studying at Harvard; covers tuition, health insurance fees and a living stipend. About 15 new fellows per year.
requirements: Citizen of Australia, Canada, New Zealand or the UK; apply before entering the US and before the Harvard program starts; check official page.

name: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship
description: Master's or doctoral fellowship (up to 24 months) at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa covering tuition, fees, housing, partial insurance and a partial stipend.
requirements: Citizens of Pacific and Asian countries (and US citizens/permanent residents); master's or doctoral; deadline Dec 1; check official page.

name: ADB-Japan Scholarship at East-West Center
description: Master's scholarship (up to 24 months) with a leadership certificate for citizens of Asian Development Bank developing member countries; covers tuition, housing, insurance, books, stipend and airfare.
requirements: Citizen of an ADB developing member country; master's level; deadline Dec 1; check official page.

name: PROGOV Fellowship (East-West Center)
description: One-year MSF, MSIS or LLM fellowship for citizens of Pacific island nations covering airfare, tuition, housing, insurance, books and stipend.
requirements: Citizen of FSM, Fiji, Kiribati, PNG, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu; deadline Mar 1; check official page.

name: Harkness Fellowships in Health Care Policy and Practice
description: Up to 12 months in the US for mid-career health services researchers and practitioners from partner countries to conduct comparative health policy work with US mentors.
requirements: Resident of Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Singapore or the UK; mid-career; check official page for application details.

name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
provider: World Bank Group / Government of Japan
description: Master's scholarships in development-related fields at participating universities (including US universities) for mid-career professionals from developing countries; covers tuition, insurance, living allowance and airfare.
requirements: National of an eligible developing country; bachelor's degree at least 3 years earlier; 3+ years development-related work; unconditional admission to a participating program outside home country; check official page.

name: Inlaks Shivdasani Scholarship
description: Scholarship of up to USD 120,000 for Indian students to pursue study at top institutions in the UK, Europe or the US.
requirements: Indian passport holder resident in India; born on or after 1 Jan 1996; Indian degree with minimum grades; admission to the chosen course; some fields excluded (e.g. MBA, computer science, medicine); check official page.
income: Selection on merit; no stated income ceiling.

name: J N Tata Endowment Loan Scholarship
provider: J N Tata Endowment for the Higher Education of Indians
description: Loan scholarship for Indian graduates pursuing graduate-level study abroad.
requirements: Indian citizen; graduate of a recognised Indian university with at least 60% marks; graduate-level program abroad; age limit 45; check official page.

name: Narotam Sekhsaria Foundation Postgraduate Scholarship
description: Interest-free, repayable scholarship for academically excellent Indian students pursuing postgraduate study at leading institutions in India or abroad, including US universities.
requirements: Academic excellence; postgraduate admission; check official page for eligibility and deadlines.
income: Described by scholars as need-blind; check official page.

name: BAEF Graduate Study Fellowships (Belgian applicants)
description: Fellowships for Belgian citizens for master's, PhD, LL.M., music and MBA study in the US, with awards of up to about $72,000 for the first year.
requirements: Belgian nationality; GRE/GMAT and TOEFL/IELTS requirements; recommendation letters; most deadlines Oct 31 (MBA May 1); check official page.

name: ASF Fellowships for Advanced Study or Research in the USA
description: Fellowships for Scandinavians (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden) for graduate or post-graduate study or research in the US for up to one year, in all fields.
requirements: Citizen/resident of a Nordic country; apply through the cooperating organization in your country (Danes apply directly); check official page.

name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
provider: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and participating Dutch institutions
description: A EUR 5,000 one-off award paid in the first year to non-EEA students starting a full-time bachelor's or master's at a participating Dutch university.
requirements: Non-EEA nationality; full-time bachelor's or master's at a participating institution; meets entry requirements; no previous degree from a Dutch institution. Not a full scholarship; deadlines set by each institution - check official page.
income: Not primarily need-based; no universal household-income ceiling.

name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
provider: Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)
description: Government scholarships (CHF 2,450 per month listed) for foreign researchers and PhD-level candidates, plus art master's awards, at Swiss universities and ETH Domain institutions.
requirements: Mainly early-career researchers with a master's degree and a Swiss academic supervisor; listed maximum age 35; art scholarships are for initial master's in artistic fields from a limited set of countries; 183 countries listed as eligible, check official page for your country and the nominating process.

name: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Programme
provider: Campus France (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs)
description: French government programme to attract foreign master's and PhD students in priority fields, with applications submitted by French institutions on the student's behalf.
requirements: Only applications submitted by French higher-education institutions are accepted; age up to 29 for master's and 35 for PhD; fields and rules set in the annual Eiffel rules - check official page.

name: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme
description: Hungarian government scholarship giving full tuition coverage and accommodation support at participating Hungarian universities.
requirements: Open to students from partner countries; levels and eligible countries depend on the annual call and your national partner agency - check official page.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships
provider: European Commission (EACEA), awarded by individual joint master's consortia
description: Each Erasmus Mundus Joint Master may offer full scholarships covering participation costs plus travel, visa and living allowance for top-ranked applicants worldwide.
requirements: Bachelor's degree or final year of bachelor's; apply directly to the chosen master's consortium, usually October to January; criteria vary by programme - check official page and the EACEA catalogue.

name: DAAD Doctoral Programmes in Germany
description: DAAD funding for doctoral studies in Germany: EUR 1,300 per month plus insurance, travel and research allowances, for up to four years.
requirements: Above-average master's or Diplom (exceptionally bachelor's); generally graduated within the last six years; doctorate begun no more than 3 years earlier; not in Germany more than 15 months at the deadline; medicine, vet and dentistry have separate rules.

name: DAAD Research Grants - Short-term (Doctoral Candidates and Postdocs)
description: Research stays in Germany of 2 to 12 months for doctoral candidates enrolled abroad, funded by DAAD.
requirements: Doctoral student outside Germany (doctorate begun no more than 3 years ago) or postdoc within 4 years of the doctorate; not resident in Germany for more than 15 months; host supervisor in Germany required - check official page.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Postgraduate Studies in Music
description: Monthly EUR 934 DAAD scholarship for master's or postgraduate study at a German college of music, with travel, insurance and language support.
requirements: First university degree in music (generally no more than 6 years old); not in Germany more than 15 months; admission to a college of music (entrance exam) is separate; tuition fees not covered.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Postgraduate Studies in Architecture
description: Monthly EUR 934 DAAD scholarship for a master's or one-year complementary course in architecture and related design fields in Germany.
requirements: First degree in architecture or related field (generally within 6 years); not in Germany more than 15 months; programme must include enough design credits; German B1 minimum for German-taught courses; tuition fees not covered.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines
description: DAAD scholarship for graduates of any discipline to complete a master's programme in Germany.
requirements: Eligibility, eligible countries and deadlines vary - check official page.

name: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (Master's Scholarships for Public Policy and Good Governance)
description: DAAD master's scholarships for public policy and good governance at selected German universities, for applicants from developing countries.
requirements: Applicants from a list of eligible countries with a first degree and professional experience; check official page for the country list and deadlines.

name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
description: DAAD scholarships for master's courses in Germany with a development-policy focus, for graduates from developing and emerging countries.
requirements: Applicants from eligible countries; usually a degree plus relevant professional experience - check official page for the list of courses, countries and deadlines.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Postgraduate Studies in the Field of the Performing Arts
description: DAAD scholarship for postgraduate study in the performing arts at a German institution.
requirements: Check official page for eligibility and deadlines.

name: Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung International Scholarship Programme
description: Scholarship for non-EU international students and doctoral candidates in Germany: up to EUR 992 per month (bachelor's/master's) or up to EUR 1,400 (doctoral).
requirements: Non-EU; B2 German; bachelor's applicants after 2 semesters in Germany; master's in a four-semester programme; no age limit; medicine and three-semester programmes not funded; domestic deadline July 15 - check official page.

name: Heinrich Boell Foundation Scholarship for International Graduate and PhD Students
description: Scholarships for master's and PhD students from DAC countries who plan to study in Germany.
requirements: First degree completed abroad; priority to applicants from DAC countries not yet in Germany; deadlines listed for spring and fall rounds - check official page.

name: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Scholarship for Foreign Students
description: Scholarship for foreign students already studying in Germany: EUR 992 per month for students or EUR 1,500 for postgraduates, plus allowances.

name: TUM Scholarship for International Students

requirements: Check official page for eligibility.

name: Lund University Global Scholarship

name: EPFL Master Excellence Fellowships
